reason: net44 is only connected to C0 and R2, so it doesn’t drive any other node in the amplifier. Removing R2 (and effectively leaving C0 connected to a floating node) eliminates an auxiliary RC path that is likely for shaping/compensation rather than core differential operation.
impact_estimate: Low (main signal path unchanged); caveat: may alter frequency response/noise if C0/R2 were intended as a compensation or filter network.

reason: C0 connects VOUT1 to net44, which otherwise only goes to R2 to ground; this looks like an optional output RC load/compensation element rather than something required for DC biasing or small-signal gain. Deleting C0 removes that extra pole/zero without breaking the biasing of the amplifier core.
impact_estimate: Low-to-Moderate; caveat: stability/transient response could change if this capacitor was providing phase lead/lag compensation (especially if the amp is used in feedback).

reason: R3 is a shunt load on the output; many amplifier cores will still bias and operate without an explicit resistive load, relying on transistor currents and any external load. Removing it mainly increases output impedance/loading headroom but does not disable the differential pair/current mirror action.
impact_estimate: Low (for functional/DC operation); caveat: output common-mode, swing, and gain under load will change, and simulations may show a different operating point if the output otherwise floats in your testbench.
